correctness.rationale: For any finite nonnegative directed row Laplacian, I+L(t) is a nonsingular M-matrix. The inverse column for vertex a has a strict maximum at a, hence d=H_aa−H_ba>0. Sherman–Morrison expresses all n single-vertex benefit scores as affine functions of the common strictly increasing scalar u=t/(1+dt). Each affine line has connected strict-winning locus, giving at most n−1 switches. For each m=n−2≥2, direct backward elimination on the acyclic graph supplies all candidate lines exactly; their slopes and adjacent crossings strictly increase. The nonadjacent-crossing weighted-mean argument proves all n lines occur successively on the envelope. Explicit positivity and rational innate-opinion checks cover all m. Independent exact-rational inverse checks for m=2,…,17 support the algebra without replacing the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Repeated selection of a best vertex to change after modifying one social tie is a natural robustness question for optimal opinion interventions. The result gives an exact global worst-case transition count and an all-sizes construction attaining it even on a directed acyclic graph. The construction shows a policy can pass through every vertex as a unique optimum, ruling out uniform robustness limits; the nonreentry theorem is an additional structural constraint. This is materially more than the standard rank-one update or a routine single instance.
